verdicts.why: Born Again S1#8 leaves them enemies: Dex escapes Rikers and aims at Vanessa, then Fisk, at the Gracie Mansion ball. The hire is backstory, so boss is wrong from here.
S1#9 shows the hire only in flashback; in the present Dex has just tried to kill the Fisks and goes on to hunt them, so the through-line is enemy.
Ridley only leads the precinct, agrees to Mariah's deal and arrives with a warrant after Bushmaster is gone (S2#9); they never meet and nothing passes between them.
In 'Straighten It Out' (Luke Cage S2#2) Bushmaster buys nightshade from Tilda at Mother's Touch; he later recognizes her from the shop, so the connection starts there.
In 'On and On' (S2#7) Bushmaster has Tilda and Mariah tied up, cuts Tilda loose, gives her the choice to save her mother and sets the house on fire. A clear turn with no stage.
In 'The Inside Man' (AoS S3#12) Hunter distrusts and tails Creel, Creel knocks him out to protect his search for Talbot's son, then saves him from a Hydra ambush; Hunter says they are not even.

In S1#8 Hoffman poisons Blake in the hospital and the masked Matt knocks him out; stage 0 (S1#13) already refers to the killing. Note they also first meet in S1#1, when Matt and Foggy get Karen released from Hoffman and Blake.
Daredevil S1#8: after Hoffman poisons Blake, the masked man knocks Hoffman out and the dying Blake gives him Fisk's plans before he dies. A death with something passing between them.
Plain typo: the stray comma makes the sentence ungrammatical. The facts are right (Bullseye kills Foggy at Cherry's retirement party at Josie's in S1#1).
Not an error: the retirement party is in S1#1, and the season-level title already starts the stage at S1's first episode, so it is not early. Adding the number changes nothing factual.
Not an error: Matt hires Cherry to look into Fisk's finances in S1#1, and the season-level title already starts there. Adding the number changes nothing factual.

In 'Shoot the Moon' (S2#2) Cashman tells Fisk that Cherry is in the hospital after the AVTF beating, and Fisk orders Powell to handle him there. The officers sent are killed, and Cherry's police friends hide him.
Not an error: Cherry learns Matt is Daredevil, keeps the secret and becomes his investigator in S1#1, and the season-level title already starts there.

In Jessica Jones S1#13 Claire treats Luke, takes him to Jessica's apartment, drains fluid from his brain during a seizure, and tells him when he wakes that he and Jessica make a good couple. This is before Luke Cage S1.
Nothing romantic happens in S1#10 (the Georgia trip). Claire turns down his coffee offer in S1#6, and in S1#13 they flirt and she kisses him before the marshals take him away.
Bakuto holds his swords to Claire's neck and cuts off Misty's arm when she charges in, in 'The Defenders' (The Defenders#8). The season-level title starts the stage too early.
In 'The Southern Cross' (S2#8) North refuses Powell's order to fire on the police at Fisk's locked-down courthouse, knocks him out and lets the crowd in, which leads to Fisk's fall.

value.title: Iron Fist S1#11
value.text: Danny learns that Colleen belongs to Bakuto's faction of the Hand and breaks with her. She turns against Bakuto, and Danny comforts her and takes her back.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Colleen's boyfriend and fighting partner, who forgives her for hiding that she belongs to the Hand.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Danny's girlfriend, who hid that she belongs to the Hand, then turns against it.

verdicts.why: The rift is real, but S1#10 leaves them apart: Danny storms off and Colleen runs the other way. They reconcile in S1#11, when she turns on Bakuto and Danny comforts her. One stage at S1#11 keeps the kind true.

They meet only in The Defenders#1, where Elektra kills Shaft while Colleen stays with him and Danny gives chase. They never speak or fight, and Colleen is elsewhere in Elektra's later scenes. One shared fight is not a connection.

value.text: Colleen draws the rest of the Iron Fist out of Davos and becomes the new Iron Fist. She and Danny part with a last kiss, and he leaves New York.
value.on_a_card_about_b: Colleen's ex-boyfriend, who helps her take the Iron Fist, then leaves New York.
value.on_b_card_about_a: Danny's ex-girlfriend, whom he helps take the Iron Fist before he leaves.

verdicts.why: Yes. In S2#10 they agree to be honest with themselves, kiss one last time and part, and Danny leaves New York with a letter saying he loves her. The S2#7 'separation' is only fandom's reading of a training rule, so stages 1 and 2 stay as they are.

In 'Heart of the Dragon' (Iron Fist S2#5) Walker fights Colleen at Joy's apartment and is about to drive a machete into her throat when Misty holds her at gunpoint and cuffs her. Then they take Walker and Joy to the dojo.

In S1#2 Ward offers Colleen money to sign a statement against Danny. She visits Danny at Birch, then hands the papers back and glares at Ward. In S1#3 Ward's men break into her dojo. They only ally in S1#13.

The Seagate flashbacks in 'Step in the Arena' (Luke Cage S1#4) show Shades and Comanche together as Rackham's enforcers. They ambush Lucas in his cell and later beat him with steel weapons. Real flashbacks count.

In S1#3 Colon accuses Cottonmouth of breaking his word on the Hammer gun sale, demands a refund or the guns and leaves threatening him; they are at war. The dispute is over guns, and their childhood tie is only shown in S1#7. (They first meet in S1#1, at the partnership talk.)
Turk is a Hell's Kitchen crook only visiting Harlem in S1#2, and Misty tells him to go back there. After Tone's death he says he is going back to Hell's Kitchen.
In 'The End' (AoS S5#22) Coulson refuses the Centipede serum and hides it in Daisy's gauntlets while urging her to face Talbot, then says goodbye and leaves with May for Tahiti.

In the last scene of 'World's End' (AoS S4#22) Enoch's soldiers storm Rae's Restaurant and Enoch freezes Coulson's team, Daisy included, and has them taken away. Nothing shown there makes him anything but an abductor.

In 'Stolen' (AoS S7#10) S.H.I.E.L.D. keeps Jiaying at the Lighthouse, and Daisy spends time with her without saying she is her daughter. Nathaniel then tells Jiaying the truth and kills her. She is on screen in S7#8 and S7#10.
Blake is killed by Cashman in S2#7 (stage 3) and appears in S2#8 only in a photo and in mentions. BB's broadcast is a third person acting after his death.

No. Skye only mentions an unseen source called Micro in AoS S2#7, and The Punisher never links Lieberman to Skye or the Rising Tide. The fandom merge cites only that mention, so on screen these two never know each other.
When the Northern Star capsizes, Fisk calls it a terrorist attack by Daredevil and orders Blake to get that out, in 'The Northern Star' (S2#1).
Danielle is on screen only in Born Again S2#6 and S2#8, and Dorothy, already dead, is in neither. A family tie on paper with no meeting.
Danielle is on screen only in Born Again S2#6 and S2#8, and James Lucas, who died in Luke Cage S2, is in neither. A blood tie never met.
Danielle is on screen only in Born Again S2#6 and S2#8, and Trish is in neither. A family tie on paper with no meeting.
Luke is not in S2#6 (only Jessica and Danielle face Mr. Charles's men). He is named as her father in S2#7 and reunites with her in S2#8, which stage 1 covers. Stage 0 has nothing between them.
Danny fights the Veznikovs, the Bride of Nine Spiders and Scythe one after another in 'Immortal Emerges from Cave' (Iron Fist S1#6). The season-level title starts the stage too early.
Same fight: Danny beats Scythe last, refusing to kill him, in 'Immortal Emerges from Cave' (Iron Fist S1#6).
Same fight: Andrei and Grigori Veznikov are Danny's first opponents in 'Immortal Emerges from Cave' (Iron Fist S1#6).
